action_text: Drink 16oz of cold water and eat a protein-rich snack like almonds, cheese, or peanut butter.
rationale: Low blood sugar mimics physical anxiety and dopamine cravings. Fueling your body stabilizes nervous system triggers.

action_text: Prepare a warm cup of herbal tea and focus solely on the sensation of warmth in your hands.
rationale: Warm liquids trigger the parasympathetic rest-and-digest response, reducing physiological tension.

action_text: Eat something with intense flavor—a slice of lemon, a pickle, or a mint. Chew slowly for 60 seconds.
rationale: Strong gustatory sensations shock the sensory cortex and interrupt obsessive behavioral feedback loops.

action_text: Eat a balanced solid meal. Step away from all screens while you eat.
rationale: Mindful eating engages the enteric nervous system and halts fight-or-flight panic driven by hypoglycemia.

action_text: Put an ice cube in your mouth. Let it melt completely without biting it while drinking a glass of cold water.
rationale: Somatic temperature disruption forces immediate nervous system regulation through the mammalian dive reflex.

action_text: Do 20 vigorous jumping jacks or pushups against a wall to release adrenaline.
rationale: Physical exertion metabolizes excess cortisol and epinephrine generated by anger.

action_text: Grab a piece of scrap paper and write down everything you are furious about. Then tear it into tiny shreds.
rationale: Externalizing rage kinesthetically provides symbolic catharsis without destructive real-world fallout.

action_text: Clench both fists as tightly as possible for 10 seconds, then completely release. Repeat 3 times.
rationale: Progressive muscle relaxation releases neuromuscular tension held during emotional flare-ups.

action_text: Step outside immediately. Walk at a brisk pace for 10 minutes without looking at your phone.
rationale: Changing your physical geography removes immediate anger stimuli and engages bilateral brain stimulation.

action_text: Send a simple check-in text to a friend, sponsor, or family member: 'Thinking of you, hope you're having a good day.'
rationale: Outward-focused connection shifts the brain out of self-isolation and activates social safety circuits.

action_text: Call your sponsor or a recovery support line right now. You do not have to know what to say.
rationale: Vocal interaction activates the ventral vagal complex, rapidly reducing feelings of acute isolation.

action_text: Open a virtual or local recovery meeting finder and join an open session immediately.
rationale: Immersing in a recovery community replaces isolation with shared purpose and mutual safety.

action_text: Splash cold water on your face, wrists, and the back of your neck.
rationale: Cold cutaneous stimulation activates sympathetic alertness and increases cerebral blood flow.

action_text: Lie down, close your eyes, and set a timer for a 20-minute power nap or non-sleep deep rest (NSDR).
rationale: Exhaustion erodes prefrontal willpower; a brief neurological reset restores impulse control capacity.

action_text: Turn down the lights, put your phone away, and prepare your bed for sleep.
rationale: Many urges are simply fatigue in disguise. The urge will pass once your body receives restorative rest.

action_text: Look around you and name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, and 1 good thing about yourself.
rationale: The 5-4-3-2-1 somatic grounding method anchors awareness in the present moment, halting panic spirals.

action_text: Complete 4 rounds of box breathing: Inhale 4s, Hold 4s, Exhale 4s, Hold 4s.
rationale: Equalized respiratory rhythm down-regulates amygdala hyperactivity and lowers heart rate variability stress.

action_text: Drop your shoulders away from your ears, unclench your jaw, and uncurl your toes. Breathe out completely.
rationale: Conscious release of physical guarding signals safety to the primitive survival brain.

action_text: Remind yourself: 'I only have to stay clear for the next 15 minutes.' Set a 15-minute timer.
rationale: Time horizon contraction prevents the brain from being overwhelmed by the weight of forever.

action_text: Look back at your cumulative days clear. That progress is permanent and cannot be erased.
rationale: Objective visual evidence of past success refutes catastrophic all-or-nothing cognitive distortions.

action_text: Call or text 988 or SAMHSA 1-800-662-4357 right now. You are worthy of support.
rationale: Professional crisis counselors provide non-judgmental presence to carry you through deep despair.

action_text: Urge Surfing: Picture the craving as an ocean wave. It rises, peaks, and naturally breaks within 15 minutes.
rationale: Urges are neurochemical surges that naturally decay when observed with curiosity rather than struggle.

action_text: Change your physical posture: Stand tall, stretch your arms overhead, and look up at the sky or ceiling.
rationale: Postural expansion alters endocrine feedback and breaks habitual physical triggers associated with urges.

action_text: Get up and move to a different room right now. Do not stay in the spot where the urge hit you.
rationale: Physical environmental transitions disrupt conditioned behavioral cue responses.
